nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH shows aggregated irregular nanowires. NiFeZn-LDH evolves into nanosheets structure with thickness ≈5 nm. NiFeOOH-V_Zn maintains nanosheets structure after electrochemical activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the as-fabricated samples was first characterized by scanning electron microscope (SEM). As shown in Figure S1 ... NiFeOOH-V_zn also demonstrate nanosheets structure

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeZn-LDH nanosheets have thickness of ≈5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the morphology of NiFeZn-LDH ... evolves into nanosheets structure with a thickness of ≈5 nm according to the atomic force microscope (AFM) images

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH shows irregular aggregated nanowires. NiFeZn-LDH shows ultrathin nanosheets with lattice fringe of 0.258 nm corresponding to (012) plane. NiFeOOH-V_Zn shows nanosheets with interplanar spacing of 0.219 nm assigned to (104) planes of NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further study the structure and morphology of them, the transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was applied. ... HR-TEM presents an interplanar spacing of 0.219 nm assigned to the (104) planes of NiOOH

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeLDH shows lattice fringe of 0.197 nm corresponding to (018) plane. NiFeZn-LDH shows lattice fringe of 0.258 nm (012) plane. NiFeOOH-V_Zn shows 0.219 nm (104) NiOOH. Post-NiFeOOH-V_Zn shows 0.239 nm (011) NiOOH and 0.219 nm (140) FeOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HR-TEM image ... exhibit a lattice fringe of 0.197 nm corresponding to the (018) crystal plane of NiFeLDH. ... lattice fringe of 0.258 nm (Figure 2c) corresponding to the (012) crystal plane

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeZn-LDH shows uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, Zn, O. NiFeOOH-V_Zn shows uniform Ni, Fe, O distribution with Zn almost non-existent. Post-NiFeOOH-V_Zn shows uniform Fe, Ni, O with no Zn.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2d shows the high-angle annular dark-field (HAADF) image and the corresponding elemental mapping images of Ni, Fe, Zn, and O ... demonstrating that these four elements are uniform distribution

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeZn-LDH has Ni:Fe:Zn atomic ratio 10.4:3.8:1. Zn completely leached from NiFeOOH-V_Zn. Partial Zn etched in e-NiFeZn-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the atomic ratio of Ni:Fe:Zn is 10.4:3.8:1 (Table S1) according to the test results of inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometry (ICP-AES). ... Zn can not be detected by ICP testing either

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH shows diffraction peaks at 11.6°, 22.9°, 34.4°, 59.9°, 61.3° corresponding to (003), (006), (012), (110), (113) planes (PDF#40-0215). NiFeZn-LDH matches NiFe-LDH with small angular shift at 11.6° due to Zn doping induced lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystal structure and composition of the as-fabricated materials were analyzed via X-ray diffraction (XRD). As demonstrated in Figure 3a, the NiFe-LDH sample shows a series of diffraction peaks at 2θ values of 11.6°, 22.9°, 34.4°, 59.9°, and 61.3°

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH shows absorption bands at ≈496, 624, 901 cm^{-1} for M-O, M-O-M, O-M-O vibrations. NiFeZn-LDH shows slight shifts confirming Zn doping effect.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The formation of Zn doped NiFe-LDH was further confirmed by Fourier translation infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy ... absorption bands at ≈496, 624, and 901 cm^{-1} are attributed to the lattice vibrations of M-O, M-O-M, and O-M-O

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-LDH: Ni 2p_{3/2} 855.78 eV, Ni 2p_{1/2} 873.38 eV (Ni^{2+}); Fe 2p_{3/2} 712.08 eV, Fe 2p_{1/2} 724.88 eV (Fe^{3+}). NiFeZn-LDH: Ni 2p peaks shift -0.38 eV; Fe 2p +0.21/0.24 eV. NiFeOOH-V_Zn: Ni 2p_{3/2} +0.78 eV vs NiFeZn-LDH indicating oxidation to higher Ni valence. O 1s: M-O (529.34 eV), M-OH (530.96 eV), H2O (531.94 eV); increased S_{M-O}/S_{M-OH} ratio after Zn leaching.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution spectra of Ni 2p (Figure 3e) located at 855.78 and 873.38 eV ... the peak area ratio of S_{M-O}/S_{M-OH} (Figure 3i) indicates that Zn leaching by electrochemical activation leads to an increased conversion

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeZn-LDH reconstructs at lower potential than NiFe-LDH: stage 1 (1.12-1.62 V) Ni(OH)2 (452, 525 cm^{-1} Eg/A1g Ni^{II}-OH), FeOOH (696 cm^{-1}); stage 2 NiOOH (478 cm^{-1} Eg Ni^{III}-O, 565 cm^{-1} A1g Ni^{III}-O). Higher I_B/I_S ratio and ΔI_S/I_B indicate deeper reconstruction and γ-NiOOH formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the in situ Raman spectroscopy evolution in Figure 5b ... a higher value of I_B/I_S manifests the formation of γ-NiOOH and the presence of high oxidized Ni^{3+δ}

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-V_Zn R_ct = 5.60 Ω (lower than NiFe-LDH 10.55 Ω, RuO2 25.80 Ω) indicates superior charge transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the charge transfer resistances (R_ct) of NiFe-LDH, NiFeOOH-V_Zn, and RuO2 is 10.55, 5.60, and 25.80 Ω, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-V_Zn C_dl = 6.9 mF cm^{-2}, higher than NiFe-LDH (1.8 mF cm^{-2}) and RuO2 (4.8 mF cm^{-2}). NiFeZn-LDH shows lower Ni^{2+}/Ni^{3+} onset potential (1.42 V vs 1.46 V) and larger oxidation peak.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl value of NiFeOOH-V_Zn sample is 6.9 mF cm^{-2}, which is much higher than both NiFeLDH (1.8 mF cm^{-2}) and RuO2 (4.8 mF cm^{-2})

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFeOOH-V_Zn selected area electron diffraction verifies formation of NiFeOOH after electrochemical activation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the selected area electron diffraction (Figure 2g) also verifies the formation of NiFeOOH after electrochemical activation

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-NiFeOOH-V_Zn shows NiOOH δ(Ni-O) 470 cm^{-1}, ν(Ni-O) 552 cm^{-1}, FeOOH Fe-O 690 cm^{-1}, confirming NiFeOOH stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra at ≈470 and 552 cm^{-1} correspond to the δ(Ni-O) and ν(Ni-O) vibrational modes of NiOOH, and peak at ≈690 cm^{-1} is ascribed to the Fe-O vibrational mode of FeOOH
